name: South Africa

facts.languages: Afrikaans, English, Southern Ndebele, Northern Sotho, Southern Sotho, Swazi, Tswana, Tsonga, Venda, Xhosa, Zulu
facts.religion: Christian about 80%, traditional faiths, Muslim and Hindu minorities

system_note: Parliament elects the president, who leads the government.
snapshot: The ANC fell to 30.8 percent in the November 2026 municipal elections, its worst result ever, as the DA became the largest party in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni and coalition talks began across most big cities.
culture: South Africa has 12 official languages, including Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans and sign language. Amapiano, the log-drum house music from the townships, has become a global genre, and kwaito, gqom and choral traditions thrive. The Springboks, back-to-back rugby world champions in 2019 and 2023, unite fans across racial lines in a way few institutions do.
society: Three decades after apartheid, South Africa remains one of the world's most unequal countries, with unemployment above 30 percent. Eskom's rolling blackouts eased in 2024 but water failures are growing. Violent crime is high. It is Africa's most industrialised economy, with world-class banks and mines and deep townships.
situation: For 30 years after Nelson Mandela's election in 1994, the African National Congress governed South Africa on its own. In 2024, worn down by corruption, power cuts and unemployment above 30 percent, it lost its majority for the first time, and Cyril Ramaphosa formed a Government of National Unity with its old rival, the business-friendly Democratic Alliance, the party many black South Africans long saw as representing white interests (Friedrich Naumann Foundation). Against expectations, the coalition has mostly held. In 2026 it faces its first big test at the ballot box.

Municipal elections are on 4 November, and they matter more than usual because South Africa's cities are where government visibly fails: water cuts, collapsing roads and uncollected rubbish. The DA chose a new leader, Geordin Hill-Lewis, the mayor of Cape Town, in April, and is running former party leader Helen Zille for mayor of Johannesburg, the economic hub (Financial Mail). One poll in Tshwane, home to the capital Pretoria, had the DA on 43 percent and the ANC on 32. The ANC is squeezed from all sides: its ally the Communist Party is running separately in protest at the coalition, and Jacob Zuma's MK party and the EFF compete for its base (EWN). Analysts expect a record number of hung councils. Meanwhile, the ANC is quietly fighting over who succeeds Ramaphosa, and tensions with the Trump administration weigh on trade.
power: A parliamentary republic. The 400-member National Assembly, elected by proportional representation, elects the president, who is both head of state and government, for up to two five-year terms. The nine provinces and the municipalities have their own elected governments.
holders: President Cyril Ramaphosa (ANC), leading the Government of National Unity since 2024.

update.html: Final results of the 4 November municipal elections, declared on 8 November, gave the ANC 30.76 percent nationally, down from 45.59 percent in 2021 and its worst result since 1994, against 24.64 percent for the DA, about 9.7 percent for Jacob Zuma's MK party and about 6 percent for the EFF. The DA overtook the ANC in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni and kept the only outright metro majority, in Cape Town, while more than half of councils have no majority; MK has asked for eThekwini's results to be frozen over alleged system failures. ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula called the result 'catastrophic'. New councils must meet within 14 days to elect mayors, a test for the ANC-DA national unity government.
